- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.67) and understate when sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33).  
- Model tends to overshoot after recent spikes; reduce forecast by 5–10% in the 3–5 day window following a price peak.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., 0.00 or negative), forecasts are too optimistic — adjust downward by 3–8% for the next 7–14 days.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.  
- Forecast bias is more pronounced in early days of the 30-day window (days 1–7) — apply a 2–5% downward correction if sentiment is weak or neutral.  
- Avoid overreacting to sentiment spikes — if sentiment jumps to 0.67+ but price is falling, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
